title: Best Disability Insurance 2026: 5 Providers Compared
description: Guardian, Principal, MassMutual, Breeze, Policygenius — income protection for cardiologist, lawyer, software engineer, sales rep profiles. True own-occupation vs modified. Real quotes.
lede: Five disability insurers. Same target: replace 60% of income if you can't work. We pulled quotes for four professional profiles and tracked true own-occupation coverage vs watered-down modified.
methodology: 35yo non-smoker in four professions: cardiologist ($500k income), lawyer ($250k), software engineer ($180k), sales rep ($150k). Tracked premium, own-occ definition, elimination period, rider options.

sections.heading: Own-occupation: the critical distinction
paragraphs: TRUE own-occupation: pays benefits if you can't do YOUR specific job, even if you can do other work. A surgeon who can't perform surgery but could consult still gets full benefits.
Modified own-occupation: pays only if you can't work in ANY job suited to your education/experience. Much weaker for high-earning professionals.
True own-occ carriers: Guardian, Principal, MassMutual. Modified: most cheaper online insurers (Breeze default; true own-occ is an upgrade).

sections.heading: Real monthly premiums
paragraphs: 35yo cardiologist, $20k/mo benefit, 90-day elimination, age 65 benefit: Guardian $480, Principal $460, MassMutual $475, Breeze (modified) $310, Policygenius (lowest) $440.
35yo software engineer, $8k/mo benefit, same parameters: Guardian $145, Principal $135, MassMutual $140, Breeze $95, Policygenius $125. Modified vs true own-occ gap: ~25-50%.
Rider costs/mo: Cost of Living Adjustment +$30-60, Future Increase Option +$15-30, Catastrophic Disability +$20-40.

sections.heading: When to buy
paragraphs: Best: in your 20s-30s while healthy. Premiums lock in based on health at issue; getting disability insurance after diagnosis is impossible.
Group employer LTD vs individual: employer LTD usually pays 60% of base salary (not bonus), maxes at $10-15k/mo, modified own-occ. Individual policies fill the gap.
High-earning professionals (doctor, lawyer, engineer): individual disability is critical. Group LTD alone leaves significant uncovered income.

faqs.q: How much benefit do I need?
faqs.a: Aim 60-70% of after-tax income. Carrier max is usually 60% of pre-tax — that's the practical limit.
Office workers: maybe. Specialists (surgeons, dentists): no. The whole point of disability insurance is to protect your specialty income; modified undermines that.
Long-term is the priority (months to years). Short-term (days to weeks) is nice but emergency fund usually covers that gap.
Higher-risk professions (surgeons, dentists with vision-critical work) have higher premiums but stronger own-occ language. Office workers have lower premiums but less differentiated own-occ coverage.

guardian-individual-disability.review: Guardian Individual Disability Income is the right pick for high-earning professionals. True own-occupation, non-cancellable. Premium pricing reflects strongest contract language.

principal-individual-disability.review: Principal Individual Disability is the right pick for doctors, dentists, lawyers. True own-occ with strong specialty language. Aggressive on medical/dental cases.

mass-mutual-radius-disability.review: MassMutual Radius Choice Disability is the right pick if you value mutual company structure. Policyholders share dividends; solid own-occ language but less aggressive than Principal on medical.
cons: Less aggressive than Principal on specialists

breeze-simplified-disability.review: Breeze Simplified Disability is the right pick for fast online signup with no medical exam (for many). $50-150/mo coverage. Default modified own-occ; true own-occ is an upgrade.

policygenius-disability-marketplace.review: Policygenius Disability Marketplace is the right pick to compare multiple carriers (Guardian, Principal, MassMutual, Mutual of Omaha, others) in one application. Often finds cheapest absolute quote. 2-4 week underwriting.

recommendedFor.label: Surgeons and medical specialists protecting procedure income
recommendedFor.reason: Principal's specialty-focused true own-occ language pays full benefits if you can't perform your specific procedures, even if you can still consult.

recommendedFor.label: High-earning attorneys and partners at law firms
recommendedFor.reason: Guardian's non-cancellable contract locks in rates and true own-occ coverage, protecting the premium income lawyers can't afford to leave uninsured.

recommendedFor.label: Self-employed freelancers and independent contractors
recommendedFor.reason: Breeze's no-medical-exam online signup and lower premiums make it the fastest path to income protection for those without employer group LTD.

recommendedFor.label: First-time buyers unsure which carrier fits their needs
recommendedFor.reason: Policygenius shops 5+ carriers in a single application, giving you side-by-side quotes from Guardian, Principal, and MassMutual to find the best fit.

recommendedFor.label: Long-horizon earners who want dividend-sharing ownership
recommendedFor.reason: MassMutual's mutual company structure returns dividends to policyholders, combining solid own-occ protection with a long-term financial participation benefit.
